examples.ko: 우리 아버지의 부성애는 말없이 깊고 조용해요.
examples.en: My father's paternal love is deep and quiet, without many words.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 부성애를 주제로 한 이야기예요.
examples.en: That movie is a story about a father's love.

examples.ko: 부성애가 강한 아빠라서 딸 걱정을 많이 해요.
examples.en: He is a dad with strong paternal love, so he worries a lot about his daughter.

examples.ko: 아이를 안고 우는 모습에서 부성애를 느꼈어요.
examples.en: I felt a father's love in the way he cried while holding the child.

examples.ko: 부성애와 모성애는 표현하는 방식이 조금 달라요.
examples.en: Paternal love and maternal love are expressed in slightly different ways.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 아버지의 부성애에 많은 사람이 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: Many people shed tears at the father's love in the drama.

explain: '모성애'와 짝으로 쓰는 말이에요. 영화나 드라마 소개, 글에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '아빠의 사랑'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the counterpart of '모성애' (maternal love). You often see it in movie or drama descriptions and in writing, while in daily talk people often say '아빠의 사랑' (dad's love) instead.

examples.ko: 이 가방에는 떼어 낼 수 있는 부속물이 많아요.
examples.en: This bag has many attachments you can detach.

examples.ko: 건물의 부속물까지 모두 계약에 포함돼 있어요.
examples.en: Even the attached fixtures of the building are included in the contract.
The shed in the yard is also an appurtenance of the house.

examples.ko: 건물 부속물을 고치는 비용은 집주인이 내요.
examples.en: The landlord pays to repair the building's attached structures.

examples.ko: 설명서에 부속물 목록이 자세히 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The manual lists the attachments in detail.
The annex looks bigger than the main building.

explain: '부속품'은 기계에 딸린 작은 물건에 주로 쓰고, '부속물'은 본채에 딸린 창고나 마당 시설처럼 주된 것에 붙은 것까지 넓게 가리켜요. 건물이나 계약 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '부속품' is mostly for small items that go with a machine, while '부속물' covers anything attached to a main thing, such as a shed or yard facilities next to a house. It appears more often in talk about buildings and contracts.

examples.en: I replaced the washing machine parts with new ones.

examples.ko: 오래된 차라서 부속품 구하기가 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's an old car, so it's not easy to find parts.

examples.ko: 부속품이 하나 모자라서 조립을 못 했어요.
examples.en: One part was missing, so I couldn't assemble it.
This vacuum cleaner comes with a wide variety of attachments.

examples.ko: 부속품은 서비스센터에서 따로 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy the parts separately at the service center.

examples.ko: 가게에서 컴퓨터 부속품을 싸게 팔고 있어요.
examples.en: The store is selling computer parts cheaply.

explain: 일상에서는 '부품'이라고 더 자주 말해요. '부속품'은 본체에 딸린 것이라서 충전기, 케이블 같은 딸림 물건에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: In daily talk people more often say '부품'. '부속품' means things that go with a main body, so it can also be used for extras like chargers and cables.

examples.en: This is a side issue, so let's talk about it later.
You also need to think about the additional costs that come with it.

examples.ko: 부수적인 설명은 줄이고 핵심만 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please cut the extra explanations and just tell me the key points.

examples.ko: 그 일에는 부수적인 효과도 꽤 많았어요.
examples.en: That work also had quite a few side benefits.

examples.ko: 부수적인 일에 시간을 너무 쓰지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't spend too much time on side tasks.

examples.ko: 이 앱의 부수적 기능은 거의 안 써요.
examples.en: I hardly ever use the secondary features of this app.

explain: '부차적'과 거의 같게 쓰고, 주된 것이 아니라 따라오는 것을 말해요. '부수적인 ~' 모양으로 많이 나오고 '부수적으로'처럼 부사로도 써요. 반대로 중요한 것은 '주된', '핵심적'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '부차적' for things that come along with the main thing. It often appears as '부수적인 ~' and also as an adverb, '부수적으로'. The opposite idea is '주된' or '핵심적'.

examples.ko: 밤에 쥐가 부스럭 소리를 내서 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: A mouse made a rustling sound at night and woke me up.
I opened the plastic bag with a rustle and took out a snack.

examples.ko: 낙엽 밟는 소리가 뒤에서 부스럭 들렸어요.
examples.en: I heard the rustle of someone stepping on fallen leaves behind me.
My younger brother got up with a rustle and turned on the light.

examples.ko: 가방 속에서 부스럭 소리가 나서 열어 봤어요.
examples.en: There was a rustling sound inside my bag, so I opened it.
Something moved with a rustle in the grass.

explain: 마른 잎, 종이, 비닐처럼 바삭한 것이 스치는 소리예요. 계속 나는 소리는 '부스럭부스럭'이라고 해요. '바스락'은 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is the sound of dry things like leaves, paper or plastic rubbing together. For a continuing sound, people say '부스럭부스럭'. '바스락' feels smaller and lighter.

examples.ko: 옆자리 사람이 계속 부스럭대서 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: The person next to me keeps rustling, so I can't concentrate.
I heard someone rustling around all night.
The child rustled around under the blanket and then fell asleep.
Please don't rustle your bag in the movie theater.
A mouse was rustling in the ceiling.
What are you rustling around with in the room?

explain: '부스럭거리다'와 같은 뜻이고, '-대다'를 쓰면 말투가 조금 더 구어적이에요. 한 번이 아니라 소리가 계속 날 때 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '부스럭거리다', and '-대다' sounds a bit more colloquial. Use it when the sound keeps going rather than happening once.

examples.en: My younger brother got up slowly and rubbed his eyes.

examples.ko: 자고 일어난 머리가 부스스해서 모자를 썼어요.
examples.en: My hair was messy after sleeping, so I put on a hat.
I don't want to go to school with messy hair.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 머리카락이 더 부스스해져요.
examples.en: On rainy days my hair gets even frizzier.
Grandfather slowly pulled himself up and spoke.
My perm has loosened and my hair is frizzy.

explain: 자다 일어나 느릿느릿 움직이는 모습, 그리고 머리카락이 엉키고 정리가 안 된 모습에 써요. 머리 이야기를 할 때는 '부스스하다' 모양으로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It describes someone getting up slowly after sleeping, and also hair that is tangled and unkempt. When talking about hair, people mostly use the form '부스스하다'.

examples.en: A light drizzle has been falling since morning.

examples.ko: 부슬비 오는 날에는 우산 없이 걷기도 해요.
examples.en: On drizzly days I sometimes walk without an umbrella.
I walked slowly in the drizzle.
It's just a drizzle, so it's fine without an umbrella.
The drizzle stopped when evening came.

examples.ko: 가을 부슬비 소리를 들으면 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: Listening to the autumn drizzle makes me feel calm.

explain: 가늘고 조용하게 내리는 비예요. '이슬비', '보슬비'와 비슷하고, 갑자기 세게 오는 '소나기'와는 느낌이 반대예요.
explain_en: It is rain that falls thinly and quietly. It is similar to '이슬비' and '보슬비', and feels the opposite of a sudden heavy '소나기' shower.

examples.ko: 부실시공 때문에 새 아파트에 물이 샜어요.
examples.en: Water leaked into the new apartment because of poor construction.
Poorly built buildings carry a high risk of accidents.
The news covered the poor construction problem in detail.
The company that did the shoddy construction took responsibility.
Poor construction was suspected, so it got a safety inspection.

examples.ko: 부실시공으로 벽에 금이 가서 다시 고쳤어요.
examples.en: The wall cracked due to shoddy construction, so it was repaired again.

explain: '부실'은 튼튼하지 못하다는 말이고 '시공'은 공사를 한다는 말이라서, 자재를 아끼거나 과정을 건너뛴 공사를 가리켜요. 뉴스에서는 '부실시공 의혹'처럼 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '날림 공사'라고도 해요. '부실 시공'으로 띄어 써도 돼요.
explain_en: '부실' means not solid and '시공' means carrying out construction, so the word points to work done by skimping on materials or skipping steps. News often says '부실시공 의혹' (suspected poor construction), and in daily talk people also say '날림 공사'. It can also be written with a space, '부실 시공'.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 갑자기 부아가 치밀었어요.
examples.en: Hearing that, I suddenly got worked up.

examples.ko: 친구가 약속을 또 어겨서 부아가 났어요.
examples.en: My friend broke the promise again and I got annoyed.
I held in my irritation and answered with a smile.

examples.ko: 아직도 그때 일만 생각하면 부아가 끓어요.
examples.en: I still seethe whenever I think about that time.
That dismissive tone got my blood boiling.

examples.ko: 괜히 부아가 나서 문을 쾅 닫았어요.
examples.en: I got irritated for no reason and slammed the door.

explain: 거의 '부아가 나다, 부아가 치밀다, 부아를 돋우다'처럼 정해진 모양으로만 써요. 그냥 '화'보다 속에서 분하게 끓어오르는 느낌이고, 대화에서 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 동료가 내 공을 가로채자 부아가 치밀었어요.
phrases.en: When my coworker took credit for my work, I got worked up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참기 어려운 분한 마음이 속에서 갑자기 올라올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a hard-to-bear, resentful anger suddenly rises inside you.
phrases.en_equiv: get worked up; feel one's blood boil

explain_en: It is used almost only in fixed phrases like '부아가 나다', '부아가 치밀다' and '부아를 돋우다'. It feels like resentful anger boiling up inside, more than plain '화', and is used in spoken language.

examples.en: The child clung to her mother's clothes and cried.
The moment I was about to fall, I grabbed the railing.

examples.ko: 그는 내 손을 부여잡고 고맙다고 했어요.
examples.en: He gripped my hand and said thank you.

examples.ko: 배를 부여잡은 채 웃느라 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was clutching my stomach laughing, so I couldn't speak.

examples.ko: 바람이 세서 모자를 두 손으로 부여잡아야 했어요.
examples.en: The wind was strong, so I had to hold my hat with both hands.
Please don't grab the arm of someone who's trying to leave.

explain: '잡다'보다 세게 꼭 붙드는 느낌이고, 절박하거나 감정이 실린 장면에 많이 나와요. 말할 때는 '꽉 잡다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '잡다', like holding on tightly, and it often appears in desperate or emotional scenes. In conversation people more often say '꽉 잡다'.

examples.en: It's foggy, so everything outside the window looks hazy.
My glasses fogged up quickly because of my breath.

examples.ko: 하늘이 부옇게 흐려서 비가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: The sky is hazy and gray, so it looks like rain.

examples.ko: 미세먼지로 멀리 있는 산이 부옇게 보여요.
examples.en: The distant mountains look hazy because of fine dust.
Everything was blurry in front of me, so I couldn't see well.
The window is fogged up and I can't see outside.

explain: 안개, 김, 먼지 때문에 흐릿할 때 쓰는 말이에요. '뿌옇다'는 더 센 느낌을 줘요. '부예요, 부예서, 부연'처럼 ㅎ이 빠지는 활용에 주의하세요. '부옇게', '부옇고'에서는 ㅎ이 그대로 남아요.
explain_en: It is used when things look blurry because of fog, steam or dust. '뿌옇다' feels stronger. Note the ㅎ drops in forms like '부예요, 부예서, 부연', while it stays in '부옇게' and '부옇고'.

examples.ko: 법원이 연락이 끊긴 삼촌을 부재자로 보고 재산 관리인을 정했어요.
examples.en: The court treated my uncle, who lost contact, as an absentee and appointed a property manager.

examples.ko: 예전에는 선거 때 멀리 있는 사람이 부재자 투표를 했어요.
examples.en: In the past, people living far away cast absentee ballots at elections.

examples.ko: 부재자의 재산을 관리할 사람은 법원이 정해요.
examples.en: The court decides who manages an absentee's property.

examples.ko: 예전에는 군대에 있는 사람도 부재자로 투표했어요.
examples.en: In the past, people in the military also voted as absentees.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 집을 떠난 뒤 소식이 없어서 부재자가 되었어요.
examples.en: He left home and has not been heard from, so he became an absentee.

examples.ko: 부재자 투표라는 말은 요즘 뉴스에서 거의 안 들려요.
examples.en: The term absentee voting is hardly heard in the news these days.

explain: 법에서는 살던 곳을 떠나 한동안 돌아올 가능성이 없는 사람을 '부재자'라고 해요. 예전 선거의 '부재자 투표'로도 알려진 말인데, 지금 선거에서는 '사전투표', '거소투표' 같은 말을 써요.
explain_en: In law, a '부재자' is a person who has left their home and is not likely to return for some time. It is also known from the old '부재자 투표' (absentee voting) in elections, but today's elections use terms such as '사전투표' (early voting) and '거소투표' (voting at one's place of residence).

examples.ko: 심사 결과 그 후보가 부적격자로 판정됐어요.
examples.en: After review, that candidate was judged unqualified.

examples.ko: 부적격자는 이 일을 맡을 수 없어요.
examples.en: Unqualified people can't take on this job.

examples.ko: 지원자 중 세 명이 부적격자라서 탈락했어요.
examples.en: Three of the applicants were unqualified, so they were eliminated.

examples.ko: 부적격자를 미리 걸러 내는 절차가 필요해요.
examples.en: We need a process to screen out unqualified people in advance.
The company keeps a separate list of ineligible people.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 부적격자라는 말에 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was surprised to hear that the person was unqualified.

explain: '적격자'의 반대말이고, 서류, 심사, 채용 같은 격식 있는 상황에서 써요. 사람에게 직접 말하면 아주 세게 들리니까 조심하세요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '적격자' and is used in formal situations like paperwork, screening and hiring. Saying it directly to a person sounds very harsh, so be careful.

examples.ko: 아빠와 아들이 걷는 모습까지 똑같네요. 부전자전이에요!
examples.en: Even the way father and son walk is the same. Like father, like son!
Being bad at singing must run in the family, from father to son.
They say like father, like son, and he cooks well just like his dad.

examples.ko: 두 사람 웃는 얼굴을 보면 부전자전이라는 말이 맞아요.
examples.en: Seeing their smiles, the saying 'like father, like son' is true.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 다들 늦잠을 자요. 이것도 부전자전일까요?
examples.en: Everyone in my family sleeps in. Is this a father-to-son thing too?
Like father, like son, his son loves soccer too.

explain: 아들이 아버지를 닮았을 때 쓰고, 좋은 점이든 웃긴 점이든 장난스럽게 말할 때가 많아요. 어머니와 딸이 닮은 경우에는 '모전여전'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a son resembles his father, often playfully, for good or funny traits alike. When a mother and daughter are alike, people say '모전여전'.

examples.en: The color of the outfit and the shoes clash.
In this room the furniture and wallpaper don't go together.
A mismatch between words and actions lowers trust.

examples.ko: 새 건물이 주변 마을과 부조화를 보여서 말이 많아요.
examples.en: The new building looks out of place next to the village, so people are talking.
The music and the video clashed, so it felt awkward.
Even in the mismatch, there is a certain charm.

explain: '조화'의 반대말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '안 어울리다'가 더 자연스럽고, '부조화'는 글이나 설명에서 많이 써요. 색이나 모양뿐 아니라 말과 행동이 맞지 않을 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '조화' (harmony). In daily talk '안 어울리다' sounds more natural, while '부조화' is common in writing and explanations. It covers not only colors and shapes but also words and actions that don't match.

examples.en: Countless people have struggled because of this.
There were plenty of people who didn't know that shop.
Seoul has countless great restaurants, so it's hard to choose.
They say countless students failed the exam.
Mistakes like that happen all the time.

examples.ko: 영어를 배우다 포기한 사람이 부지기수인 걸요.
examples.en: There are so many people who gave up while learning English.

explain: '아주 많다'를 조금 격식 있게 말하는 표현이에요. 보통 '~이/가 부지기수예요' 모양으로 쓰고, 좋은 일이든 나쁜 일이든 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a slightly formal way to say 'very many'. It is usually used as '~이/가 부지기수예요' and works for both good and bad things.

examples.en: Before I knew it, I had developed a bad habit.
Without realizing it, I called that person's name.

examples.ko: 부지불식간의 한마디가 상처가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A remark made unconsciously can hurt someone.
While listening to the song, tears came without my noticing.
Time slipped by before I knew it.
It was something I did unconsciously, so I don't know why.

explain: 거의 '부지불식간에' 모양으로 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '나도 모르게'라고 더 자주 말하고, '부지불식간'은 글이나 연설에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It almost always appears as '부지불식간에'. In daily talk people more often say '나도 모르게' (without realizing), while '부지불식간' shows up in writing and speeches.

examples.en: Don't just worry for nothing, take action.
I'm pointlessly going over what happened in the past.
I ended up just wasting time in vain.
I got my hopes up for no reason and ended up disappointed.

examples.ko: 부질없이 남과 비교하며 마음 상하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't hurt yourself by pointlessly comparing with others.
I just sat there sighing to no purpose.

explain: 형용사 '부질없다'의 부사형이고, 해 봐야 소용이 없다는 허무한 마음이 들어 있어요. '괜히'보다 무겁고 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is the adverb form of the adjective '부질없다' and carries a feeling of futility, that it won't help anyway. It is heavier than '괜히' and appears more in writing.

examples.ko: 한국 전통 공연에서 부채춤을 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the fan dance for the first time at a Korean traditional performance.
The fan dance goes well with colorful hanbok.
My friends performed the fan dance at the school festival.

examples.ko: 외국인 관광객이 부채춤 공연을 보고 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Foreign tourists clapped after watching the fan dance performance.

examples.ko: 부채춤에서 부채가 꽃처럼 펼쳐지는 장면이 예뻤어요.
examples.en: The scene in the fan dance where the fans open like flowers was beautiful.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 부채춤을 배운 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I learned the fan dance when I was little.

explain: '부채춤을 추다'처럼 '추다'와 함께 써요. 한복을 입고 하는 공연에서 자주 볼 수 있어서 한국 문화를 소개할 때 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used with '추다' (to dance), as in '부채춤을 추다'. You often see it in performances in hanbok, so it comes up a lot when introducing Korean culture.

examples.en: That neighborhood is a well-known wealthy area in Seoul.

examples.ko: 부촌에 사는 사람들은 집이 정말 커요.
examples.en: The people living in the wealthy area have really big houses.
This area has been known as a wealthy neighborhood for a long time.
It's near a wealthy area, so housing prices are very high.

examples.ko: 부촌과 달리 이쪽 동네는 조용하고 소박해요.
examples.en: Unlike the wealthy area, this neighborhood is quiet and modest.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 부촌 풍경이 현실과 너무 달라요.
examples.en: The wealthy neighborhood in the drama looks too different from reality.

explain: 부동산이나 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이고, 일상에서는 '부자 동네'라고도 해요. 반대로 가난한 동네는 '빈촌'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It often appears in real estate and news, and in daily talk people also say '부자 동네' (rich neighborhood). A poor neighborhood is called a '빈촌'.

examples.en: My friend lost his father, so I went to the funeral hall.
I heard about the death of his father and contacted him right away.

examples.ko: 팀장님이 부친상이라서 이번 주는 출근을 못 하세요.
examples.en: The team leader's father passed away, so he can't come to work this week.
I sent a message to comfort him over his father's death.

examples.ko: 부친상 소식을 들은 동료들이 조문을 갔어요.
examples.en: Coworkers who heard about his father's death went to pay their respects.

examples.ko: 부친상 때문에 결혼식에 못 온다고 했어요.
examples.en: He said he can't come to the wedding because of his father's death.

explain: 다른 사람 아버지의 상을 격식 있게 말할 때 써요. 보통 '부친상을 당하다'라고 하고, 어머니는 '모친상', 부모님 두 분은 '부모상'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a formal way to refer to someone else's father's death. It is usually used as '부친상을 당하다', and for a mother it is '모친상', for either parent '부모상'.
